title: Recognizing reference/sample data given in problem
trigger: When a question shows sample datasets or example data alongside the problem, treat them as reference/context for understanding the data format, not as something to compute on directly.

title: Single accumulator counting rows under AND/OR condition trace
trigger: Step through the loop row-by-row, evaluate the AND/OR boolean condition for each row against the table's fields, and increment the counter only when the condition is true; also check whether the nested condition can ever actually be satisfied, since an impossible AND combination leaves the counter stuck at zero.

title: Two accumulators tracked in parallel over nested filter branches
trigger: When a loop has nested if/else branches each updating a different accumulator (A, B), trace all counters together row-by-row in one pass rather than one variable at a time, and match each accumulator to the specific branch condition that increments it.

title: Complement counting: total minus AND-count for an OR filter
trigger: To find how many rows satisfy 'cond1 OR cond2' when you already have A = rows satisfying the AND of the negations (or another related AND-count), compute B = total_row_count - A instead of re-scanning the table with OR logic directly.

title: Single-pass running maximum/flag tracking during a bounded scan
trigger: Scan items one at a time (often capped by a loop-limit like 'first five sentences'), update a running best/flag value only when the current item beats the stored maximum so far, and recognize that this kind of max-tracking result does not depend on the original row/iteration order.

title: Implement/identify XOR of two boolean conditions
trigger: When a procedure or flag must be True only when exactly one of two conditions holds, write it as (condA and not condB) or (not condA and condB) — equivalent to condA != condB — and reject any option that just uses plain AND/OR of the two conditions.

title: Paired OR-flag and AND-count accumulators in one loop
trigger: When a loop updates two separate variables together, trace one iteration for each: a variable that is set True/incremented on 'if condA or condB' becomes True/increments as soon as EITHER condition ever holds, while one using 'if condA and condB' (or the negation of an OR) only updates when BOTH/ALL conditions hold — identify which combinator each variable's if-statement actually uses before deciding what it represents.

title: Trace a primality-test helper procedure
trigger: Recognize a doSomething(X)-style procedure that loops checking divisibility from 2 up to X-1 and returns True only if no divisor is found — it is testing primality; then trace how the caller uses this Boolean result (e.g., counting or selecting prime positions/elements) to get the final answer.

title: Two independent non-nested loops over the same list
trigger: Spot when the code runs two separate for-loops (not nested) over the same dataset, each with its own filter condition and its own accumulator — evaluate each loop's resulting variable independently by tracing it on its own, rather than assuming the two loops interact.

title: Trace a custom compound-rule procedure literally
trigger: When a procedure defines its own non-standard rule (e.g., comparing two rows for 'fairness', or checking a sequence for an alternating pattern) across multiple fields or steps, don't guess a generic pattern — trace the procedure's own logic step-by-step against the given test case to see what condition it actually enforces.

title: Nested loop sum of pairwise differences telescopes to zero
trigger: When a nested loop accumulates sum += list1[i] - list2[j] (or similar) across symmetric index ranges, trace the loop bounds once to see the differences cancel in pairs (telescoping to 0) instead of hand-simulating every iteration.

title: Pairwise (i<j) nested loop counting matches with AND/OR condition
trigger: Recognize the i<j (or all-unique-pairs) nested-loop structure that compares every pair of records once; substitute the comparison logic to see what the counter tallies — AND requires both attributes to match, OR requires only one — and count = number of pairs satisfying that condition.

title: Binning by category then counting pairs within/across bins
trigger: When records are first grouped/binned by a category (e.g., city/pile) and then nested loops count pairs restricted to the same bin vs. across different bins, keep separate counters straight: an ungrouped pairwise total vs. a same-bin-only count vs. a cross-bin-only count, and identify which loop bounds (same pile vs. different piles) each counter iterates over.

title: Shopping-Bills-style nested loop: outer counter N = trip count
trigger: In the recurring 'Shopping Bills' pseudocode, the outer loop variable N counts total outer-loop iterations (number of rows/customers scanned), independent of the inner tally — trace only the outer loop's increment to find what N equals at termination.

title: Shopping-Bills-style nested loop: inner tally count and running max A
trigger: The inner loop resets a counter to 0 and tallies matches for the current outer key (e.g., bills for this customer); after the inner loop finishes, that count is compared against a running maximum A and A updates if count > A. So count = per-key frequency and A = the largest frequency seen so far — trace count and A together across outer iterations to answer MCQ/MSQ statements about them.

title: Nested loop element-matching for duplicates or shared items
trigger: Two nested loops compare every element of one collection (list/string) against every element of another (or itself) and increment a counter only when a specific match condition holds (identical value, same character); pin down exactly what triggers the increment to identify what the final counter represents (a duplicate count, a shared-letter count, etc.).

title: Trace a list built via repeated rest()
trigger: When a loop repeatedly sets L = rest(L) (or appends rest(L) results into a new list LB), each successive element is a shrinking suffix of the original list — length(LB) grows by one per rest() call while each new element shrinks toward empty; step through first(L)/rest(L) one call at a time to answer length, emptiness, last-element, and content questions.

title: Recursive list equality via first/last/init/rest
trigger: The procedure recurses using first(L)/last(L) paired with rest(L)/init(L) to peel one element off each end (or off two lists) per call and compare them; trace which pair of elements is compared at each recursive call and what the base case requires to return True.

title: Scan a list tracking a running minimum with tie-break
trigger: Walk the list once keeping a running best value and its index; when a new candidate ties or beats the current best, apply the stated tie-break rule (e.g. closest to the first vs. last station) to decide whether the running best actually updates.

title: Trace a boolean flag set during a list scan
trigger: Simulate the loop position by position, flipping the flag only when the stated condition on the current element/position holds; the flag's final True/False value constrains which list contents are consistent with that trace.

title: Debug a sorted-list insertion (insertion sort) procedure
trigger: Check the three classic insertion-sort bugs: wrong initial value of the 'position found' flag, an off-by-one in the comparison/insert index, and a wrong comparison operator for the intended sort order (ascending vs descending) — hand-trace one insertion into a short sorted list to see which bug(s) actually break it.

title: Build a duplicate-free list via membership check
trigger: The procedure appends an item to a result list only when 'item not in resultList' — recognize this dedup guard and trace it letter-by-letter or word-by-word to see which items survive; a list that gets reinitialised (or fails to reset) inside the wrong loop is the classic bug to spot.

title: Count sentences by matches against a reference word list
trigger: For each sentence, count how many of its words are members of a fixed reference list (e.g. a positive-word list) using 'in', then increment a sentence-counter only if that count meets a threshold — trace the inner membership-count loop first, then check the outer threshold comparison.

title: Count adjacent or corresponding element matches
trigger: A loop with index i compares list[i] to a neighbour (list[i-1] or list[i+1]) or to the corresponding element of a second list, and increments a counter on a match — identify exactly which pair is being compared and where the increment belongs to fill in or evaluate the code.

title: Build a cumulative-sum list from a source list
trigger: Each new element of cumuList equals the previous cumuList element plus the current aList element (cumuList starts from aList[0]), so length(cumuList) always equals length(aList) and the last element of cumuList is the total sum — check any statement against this running-total invariant.

title: Identify what outList (a list of lists) represents
trigger: Recognize the outer-loop-over-sentences / inner-loop-over-words pattern: each sentence becomes one sublist appended to outList, possibly filtered (e.g. excluding adjectives) or reduced (e.g. to just first/last word) — match the described selection rule to the correct 'what outList represents' option.

title: Track counter A against outList/length(outList)
trigger: A separate counter A is incremented under its own condition, not simply once per sentence, so A need not equal length(outList) — trace A's increment condition and outList's append condition sentence-by-sentence to see whether and where they diverge.

title: Dictionary keys/values property statements (true/false)
trigger: When asked which statements about a dictionary D are true, check each against the core API facts: keys(D) has no duplicates, len(D)==len(keys(D))==len(values(D)), D[k] fails on a missing key unless get()/default is used, and values may repeat while keys may not — test each option against these facts rather than the specific dataset.

title: Single-level dictionary trace: what the final structure represents
trigger: Simulate the loop row-by-row on a small mental example, writing down what gets stored/overwritten/incremented at each key on each pass; the final value at a key is determined by whichever write rule (last-value-wins, running max/min, increment, invert-store) the code actually uses, not by intuition about what 'should' happen.

title: Letter-frequency dictionary: build/update and read off a count
trigger: Trace updateDict/letter-count code character by character on the exact word given, incrementing dict[letter] (initializing to 1 on first sight), then read the requested value directly off the finished dictionary or off the running max/min tracker.

title: Debug most/least-frequent-letter dictionary pseudocode
trigger: Check the four classic frequency-dictionary bugs in order: (1) missing/wrong initialization for an unseen key, (2) comparing with > vs >= (biases tie-breaking / first vs last occurrence), (3) updating the max-tracker inside the wrong loop/branch, (4) restricting to the wrong character set (e.g. vowels vs consonants vs all letters) — most MSQ answers combine two of these.

title: Debug general counting-dictionary construction pseudocode
trigger: For non-letter counting dictionaries (books per author, shop categories, station counts), check: does the code initialize a new key to 0/1 before incrementing, does it use the correct key expression (not a hardcoded/wrong field), and does the increment happen inside the right loop so every record is counted exactly once.

title: City-keyed min/max/first-last dictionary trace
trigger: Recognize a dictionary storing a growing list [first-seen, ..., last-seen or running-min/max] per city key; the queried expression (first(D[i])-last(D[i]) or similar) equals (earliest or max value) minus (latest or min value) for that key, so trace only that one key's sequence of updates rather than the whole table.

title: Per-city average vs overall-average comparison count (Z)
trigger: Recognize the two-pass pattern: pass 1 builds a dict of (sum, count) per city to get each city's average; pass 2 compares each city's average to the overall dataset average and increments Z for every city on one side of that comparison — so Z counts cities above/below the overall mean, not a total or a max.

title: Nested dictionary keyed by city + gender (or similar 2-key group)
trigger: Recognize a dictionary-of-dictionaries or tuple-keyed dictionary where the outer key is one category (city) and the inner key/second field is another (gender); trace which record updates which (outer,inner) cell, then read the requested cell or sum across inner keys for a given outer key.

title: Shop/item nested dictionary revenue tracking (itemD/costD)
trigger: Recognize itemD[shop][item] or costD[shop] style nested dictionaries built by scanning transaction records; itemD[i][j] typically accumulates total revenue for item j at shop i, while costD[i] tracks a running min/max item within shop i — identify which of the two roles the code implements by checking whether it sums or compares.

title: Word-to-sentence-count dictionary (wCount)
trigger: Recognize the 'count sentences containing word' pattern: for each sentence, first build the set of distinct words in that sentence (to avoid double-counting a repeated word within one sentence), then increment wCount[word] once per distinct word per sentence — the correct code option is the one that dedupes within-sentence before incrementing.

title: Determine edge condition from graph-building criteria
trigger: When asked what condition creates an edge between i and j, locate the exact rule that filled the matrix/graph (an equality, AND-of-attributes, or threshold test) and match it directly to the answer choices — the correct option just restates that fill rule, don't reason about the graph's overall shape.

title: Interpret what a matrix/dict entry or expression represents
trigger: When asked what matrix[i][j]=1, A[i][j], or an expression like A x y represents, trace back to the code/scenario that populated the cell and translate the row/column indices into the real-world pair being described; separately check whether the fill rule is symmetric (matrix[i][j]==matrix[j][i], undirected relation) or can differ across the diagonal (directed relation).

title: Count a node's degree from an adjacency matrix
trigger: To count edges touching a node, sum (count the 1s in) that node's row or column of the adjacency matrix, or equivalently count its neighbors listed in the adjacency list.

title: k-step path reachability via repeated matrix updates
trigger: A 'value after applying the update procedure N times' question is really computing the adjacency matrix raised to the N-th step — walk through one update call at a time, tracking exactly how each cell changes on that pass, rather than trying to jump straight to the final matrix.

title: Verify or reason about cliques in an undirected graph
trigger: A clique is a set of vertices that are ALL pairwise connected — to check a candidate clique, verify every pair among its vertices has an edge; to disprove a claim or find a bigger/smaller clique, find one missing edge (or one vertex not connected to every other member).

title: Read degree, edges, and cliques directly off a drawn graph diagram
trigger: When the graph is shown as a picture rather than a matrix or rule, answer by direct visual inspection: count line segments meeting a vertex for its degree, and check pairwise connections among candidate vertices for clique statements — no matrix construction needed.

title: Symmetric comparison-matrix from equality/range condition
trigger: M[i][j] is defined by a symmetric condition (e.g. |value_i - value_j| <= k, or value_i == value_j) - since the condition holds equally for (i,j) and (j,i), the matrix is symmetric, the diagonal is fixed by self-comparison, and the total sum of entries = 2 x (number of qualifying pairs); check these structural facts before evaluating individual answer statements.

title: Directed comparison-matrix from strict inequality, find extremal node
trigger: M[i][j] is defined by a strict directional condition (e.g. value_i > value_j) - so M[i][j] and M[j][i] can never both be 1 (asymmetric), the diagonal is always 0, and a node whose entire row is 1 (or whole column is 0) is the max/min scorer; scan rows/columns for all-1 or all-0 patterns to find that node.

title: Weighted directed tournament matrix from contest results
trigger: The matrix stores a directed, weighted result of pairwise contests (e.g. chess match winner/margin) - matrix[i][j] and matrix[j][i] are sign-opposite (or one is set, other 0), and a row/column of all zeros identifies a player who was never beaten (zero in-degree); read the construction rule first, then check rows for all-zero patterns.

title: Multi-category co-occurrence matrix (qualifies in every list)
trigger: The matrix entry is built by scanning each entity's list/dict and marking a pair only if their shared-attribute condition holds across EVERY category (all subjects, all books, all lists) simultaneously - trace the nested loop over categories for the specific pair/entry asked about rather than checking a single comparison.

title: Row-scan procedure trace (Dosomething/checkSomething on one row)
trigger: Dosomething(M,i)/checkSomething(B,i) only ever reads row i (or column i) of the matrix and returns a count or True/False from that single row's pattern - simulate by extracting just row i from the given matrix and counting or checking entries directly; other rows are irrelevant.

title: updateMatrix single pass: one-hop-extended (2-step) reachability
trigger: updateMatrix(M) sets newMatrix[p][q]=1 if there exists some intermediate k with M[p][k]=1 AND M[k][q]=1 (one BFS-style hop added to existing edges) - for the queried p,q, search for any k satisfying both conditions in the given matrix; this single call captures reachability within 2 steps.

title: updateMatrix applied twice: multi-hop (3+ step) reachability
trigger: Applying updateMatrix a second time feeds the first call's output matrix back in, extending reachability by one more hop - first compute the intermediate matrix from call 1 (2-step reachability), then re-apply the same k-exists rule using that intermediate matrix to get the final p,q values (3-4 step reachability).

title: Nested-loop counting of fixed-length paths, triangles, or cycles
trigger: A triple (or quadruple) nested loop that increments 'count' whenever a product/chain of matrix entries like M[i][j]*M[j][k]*M[k][i] equals 1 is counting closed walks/triangles (3 loops) or longer fixed-length paths (4 loops) - identify loop depth to know what's being counted, then manually enumerate matching index tuples on the small given graph.

title: Mixed / one-off
trigger: Non-recurring pattern - work through the specific pseudocode (ijMin minimum-distance procedure) line by line against the given matrix to find each stated mistake; no shared technique with other archetypes this week.

title: DFS traversal trace on adjacency matrix
trigger: Manually simulate the DFS recursion with a visited set, appending each node to L the instant it is first visited (pre-order); scan each row of the adjacency matrix in index order to pick the next unvisited neighbor before backtracking.

title: DFS parent-dictionary key-order trap
trigger: Recognize that dictionary keys() are listed in insertion order (the order a node was first assigned a parent during DFS), not sorted or visit-completion order — trace when each key gets ADDED, not when the node finishes.

title: Recursive trace on two integers (Euclidean-style)
trigger: Find the base case (an argument hits 0 or the two arguments become equal) and hand-unwind the calls, substituting the swapped/reduced pair (e.g. (a,b)->(b, a-b) or (a,b)->(b, a%b)) at each step exactly like tracing Euclid's GCD.

title: Recursive digit sum via mod and integer division
trigger: Recognize DoSomething(n) = n%10 + DoSomething(n//10) with base case n==0 — peel off the last digit each call with % and shrink n with // , summing digits as the recursion unwinds.

title: Counting recursive calls over a list
trigger: One recursive call is made per remaining element until the base case fires, so the call count equals the list length — check whether the question counts the initial call or excludes it (off-by-one).

title: Single-list recursion consuming one element per call (first + rest)
trigger: Recognize the pattern first(L) combined-with recurse(rest(L)), base case = empty list — at each level compare/combine only the current first element with the recursive result on the tail, one element consumed per call.

title: Single-list recursion peeling both ends (first & last together)
trigger: Recognize recursion that removes the FIRST and LAST elements in the same call, combining/comparing them and recursing on the INIT-minus-first (or middle) sublist — base case is an empty or single-element list; track which two elements are paired at each level.

title: Recursive list reversal via first/last/init/rest
trigger: To reverse a list recursively, the correct fragment appends the current first element to the END of reverse(rest(L)) — check each candidate fragment against this reverse(rest)+[first] shape rather than first+reverse(rest).

title: Recursive dual-list pairwise combination (product/sum)
trigger: Recognize recursion advancing two lists in parallel — combine first(L1) with first(L2) via + or *, add/accumulate into S, and recurse on rest(L1), rest(L2); base case is when either list is empty, so trace S level by level.
